brief: Cuts a list into parts: at an item, at positions, before or after one, into n parts, into parts of n items, by a condition or at a pace.
detail: It is the cutting helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its Split, SplitXT, SplittedXT, SplittedAsSectionsXT and SplittedAtPositions methods; build one with new stzListSplits when you only need to cut. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed. The answer is a list of parts, each part a list. Unlike the split of a text, a cut item is not thrown away: it is kept and starts the next part, and a cut at position 1 or past the end adds no empty part. A verb (Split, SplitAt, SplitBefore ...) cuts the held list in place and returns nothing, so read Content afterwards, its Q form returning the splitter for chaining; the Splitted forms return the parts and leave the splitter alone. SplitXT and SplittedXT take the options in one argument (a position, a list of positions, or a pair such as [ :After, 3 ] or [ :ToNParts, 3 ]), and SplittedAsSectionsXT answers the [ first, last ] positions of the parts. A number is always read as a position, never as an item, so a list of numbers cannot be cut at one of its items. SplitAfter with an item cuts only after its last occurrence. A pace of 0 in SplitAtPacer never ends.
